edition.locus: Gebhardt II.1-4 (brought before the proconsul at Pergamum)

source_text: Ἐνδημοῦντος τοῦ ἀνθυπάτου ἐν Περγάμῳ προσήχθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μακάριοι Κάρπος καὶ Παπύλος, μάρτυρες τοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ὁ δὲ ἀνθύπατος προκαθίσας ἔφη· Τί καλεῖ; Ὁ δὲ μακάριος ἔφη· Τὸ πρῶτον καὶ ἐξαίρετον ὄνομα Χριστιανός, εἰ δὲ τὸ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ζητεῖς, Κάρπος. Ὁ ἀνθύπατος εἶπεν· Ἔγνωσται σοι πάντως τὰ προστάγματα τῶν Αὐγούστων περὶ τοῦ δεῖν ὑμᾶς σέβειν τοὺς θεοὺς τοὺς τὰ πάντα διοικοῦντας· ὅθεν συμβουλεύω ὑμῖν προσελθεῖν καὶ θῦσαι.
pass_a_gloss: While the proconsul was staying in Pergamum, the blessed Carpus and Papylus, witnesses of Christ, were led up before him. And the proconsul, having sat forward to preside, said: What are you called? And the blessed one said: The first and choice name is Christian, but if you seek the one in the world, Carpus. The proconsul said: Surely the commands of the Augusti have become known to you, concerning that you must revere the gods who administer all things; hence I counsel you to come forward and sacrifice.
pass_b_english: While the proconsul was holding court at Pergamum, the blessed Carpus and Papylus, witnesses of Christ, were brought into his presence. Once the proconsul had taken his seat on the tribunal, he asked, What is your name? The blessed man answered, My first and choicest name is Christian, but if you want the name I bear in the world, it is Carpus. The proconsul said, You surely know the decrees of the emperors, that you must worship the gods who govern all things, and so I urge you to step forward and offer sacrifice.

choices.why: plural honorific adjective attached to Carpus and Papylus in a martyr narrative, so it marks their blessed status rather than ordinary happiness
short courtroom question asking for the accused's name; the Greek asks literally what he is called, so English idiom needs the name-question form

choices.english: the name I bear in the world
choices.why: contrasted with the first and choice name Christian, so it denotes his ordinary civic name in earthly life
